title: Safety measurements – measurements of stopping time, speed, force and pressure
description: The main objective is to minimise the risk of serious injury by ensuring that the machine stops before an employee reaches a hazardous component.

blocks.text: Fractions of a second that save lives
The main objective is to minimise the risk of serious injury by ensuring that the machine stops before an employee reaches a hazardous component.
Does the machine stop in time?

items: Determining the safe distance: Checking whether the safety curtain, light barrier, scanner, USO, and non-locking limit switches are positioned at a suitable distance from the hazard zone. If the machine stops too slowly, the operator may reach into the hazardous area before it has come to a complete stop.
Brake verification: Checking the wear of the braking systems in machines to detect whether the machine is stopping more slowly than specified in the documentation.
Compliance with standards: A legal requirement (e.g. standard PN-EN ISO 13855) mandating periodic inspections, usually once every 12 months.
Monitoring of "safe speed": Ensuring that drives do not exceed values defined as safe, particularly in machines with speed control.
Calculation of safety distances: The approach speed of a person (or body part) is key in the formula for calculating how far from the danger zone a curtain/barrier must be positioned.

blocks.text: Reduction of impact and crushing force

items: Protection against crushing/impact: Checking that the closing force of guards or presses is not too high, which could cause injury.
Minimising the risk of failure: Monitoring pressure in pneumatic systems enables early detection of faults that could lead to sudden, uncontrolled movement of the machine.

blocks.text: In summary, these measurements are carried out to verify the effectiveness of protective measures, prevent workplace accidents, and meet legal requirements.
